title: First 5 Minutes: Developer Onramp Voice Experiments
content:
Purpose:
Capture a set of short, developer-facing messaging drafts and quickstart flows that are focused on the literal first 5 minutes a new dev spends with Redwood Hosted API. We want testable microcopy, pricing hooks, and success metrics that reduce perceived friction and accelerate a dev from signup -> first meaningful response (and ultimately first production call).

Context + problem statement:
- We believe the biggest blocker for PLG adoption is early friction: unclear cost expectations, too many knobs to configure, and documentation that assumes architecture knowledge.
- Existing collateral leans technical but often buries the single-sentence value prop and immediate next step.
- Hypothesis: an explicit “first-5-minutes” path (short checklist + microcopy) reduces time-to-first-call and increases conversion to paid by improving perceived safety on cost and speed-to-result.

Primary hypotheses to test (ranked):
1) Transparent per-call unit examples (mini bill) reduce anxiety more than discounts/free credits alone.
2) 1-click starter with a pinned small model + sample prompt beats open-ended model selection for time-to-first-call.
3) Pricing language that ties to expected token counts (e.g., “~$0.02 for 100 prompt+response tokens”) is understood faster than abstract cents-per-token.

Key metrics (what to measure in the first experiments):
- Time from signup -> API key created (target: <3 min)
- Time from signup -> first successful text generation call (target: <5 min)
- % of devs who run the sample integration in the quickstart (goal +30% vs baseline)
- Conversion to paid within 30 days for those who hit first-call (compare cohorts)

Quickstart flows (3 concise patterns to prototype):
A) Minimal starter ("Run in 60s"):
  - Button: Run a sample request (no model choice, no config).
  - Behind-the-scenes: issues a request against a low-cost small model with streaming enabled.
  - Microcopy above button: "See a response in 60s — no config required. We'll show cost estimate first."

B) Guided sample with cost preview ("How much will it cost?"):
  - Short slider to pick expected response length (100/300/800 tokens), UI shows estimate: "~$0.02 / $0.06 / $0.16".
  - After slider, a single sample request button.
  - Microcopy: "Estimate is per response; we'll warn if you exceed your daily free credits."

C) Code-first quickstart ("Paste and run"):
  - Pre-filled snippet in Python/JS that uses the hosted endpoint + API key.
  - Snippet chosen by default to call a pinned example prompt and print token/cost breakdown.
  - Microcopy next to snippet: "Copy, paste, run. First request costs ~$0.02 — safety caps included."

Microcopy experiments (variants to A/B):
- Headline variants (short):
  1) "Start building — see output in 60s"
  2) "Your first inference, in one click"
  3) "Try Redwood: free tier + predictable cost estimates"
- CTA variants:
  1) "Run sample (no config)"
  2) "Try now — estimate cost"
  3) "Copy code and run"
- Pricing phrasing variants:
  1) Units-first: "Estimate: ~ $0.02 for a 150-token request (prompt + response)"
  2) Safety-first: "Free credits + daily cost cap. You control spend from day one."
  3) Simplified monthly anchor: "Most devs spend < $10/month in prototyping"

Pricing-language drafts (short paragraphs we can drop into UI or emails):
- Variant P1 (transparent, technical): "Redwood charges per token for generation and per vector for embeddings. For prototyping, expect a small response to cost about $0.02 (a 100-token prompt + 50-token response). We’ll always show an estimate before you run a call and enforce your account caps unless you opt out."

- Variant P2 (developer reassurance): "Start for free with $50 credits and built-in spend caps. We’ll show a clear cost estimate before any call so you never get surprised. When you’re ready, scale with predictable per-token pricing and optional reserved capacity."

- Variant P3 (value-first): "Get to a working prototype quickly: sample prompts, pre-configured SDKs, and cost estimates built into every quickstart. Production teams use Redwood to make inference predictable and economical — start small, control spend, scale when ready."

Instrumentation & A/B plan:
- Run 3 micro-experiments on the quickstart landing: (1) Minimal starter CTA vs (2) Cost-preview CTA vs (3) Code-first CTA. Randomize by user cookie.
- Track heatmap of where users hesitate: api key creation, model selection, 'estimate cost' modal.
- Funnel events: page view -> create account -> create api key -> run sample -> view cost modal -> upgrade CTA click.

Edge cases & safety copy (must include):
- Cost caps language: short line in footer of quickstart: "Daily cap: $X (set in Console) — you’ll never be billed over caps without confirming)."
- Auto-fallback language for out-of-quota: "If the pinned model is unavailable, we’ll route to an equivalent low-cost model — you’ll see the estimated cost first."

Open questions / decisions to make before experiment launch:
- Should the default pinned model be the smallest architecture, or a slightly higher-quality one to reduce false negatives on quality? (tradeoff: cost vs. first-impression quality)
- How big should the 'first-free credits' be? $10, $50? Bigger cap reduces churn but increases cost to us.
- Is the cost estimate shown in cents or as a qualitative label ("negligible", "small", "moderate")?

Quick tactical TODOs (1-2 week sprint):
- [ ] Implement 3 quickstart landing variants (UX + copy) — design + frontend (PR #3421)
- [ ] Backend: add cost-estimate endpoint for sample flows + cap enforcement (ticket JIRA-AI-1789)
- [ ] Instrument events and wire up dashboard to measure the funnel (product-analytics)
- [ ] Draft short email + toast nudges for users who hit first-call but did not upgrade (Priya)
- [ ] Run internal dogfood test with SRE + developer advocates (goal: 50 internal runs)

Notes / scribbles:
- Consider a tiny badge next to API key: "Estimated $0.02 per small response" — quick reassurance in the Console.
- We should avoid "free forever" language; better to emphasize predictable cost and credits.
- Example story for hero slot: "How a dev launched a Slack bot in an afternoon — cost < $15" (short case microstory)

Next steps for this doc:
- Share with solutions engineering to sanity-check dev flows (Marco)
- Get UX to design 3 low-fi variants and quick thumbs (Jordan)
- Schedule a measurement sync with analytics and infra (Priya)

Unresolved / backlog ideas:
- Explore bundling a 1-click starter that wires up a temporary webhook + sample bot for integrations (could increase time-on-platform but is more infra-costly).
- Investigate 'sandbox' keys that run in a simulated mode with unlimited small outputs (helps reduce churn but is easy to abuse).

End of draft.

-- Evelyn
(quick note: keep copy short in UI; detailed pricing lives in the pricing page linked from quickstart)
